family.note: Same InventoryMenu domain and same 3-arg (window, unused, state) signature idiom, but this owner does not draw item name text at all -- it caches page*5+entry_count into state+24, optionally draws one status message via Func_08015080 when *(u16*)(menu+combined*2+456)!=0, then runs a fixed 5-iteration loop calling Func_080a2268 (a 6-arg call, 2 args on the stack) to draw per-row markers, picking tile 14 vs 15 in the 6th argument depending on whether the row equals entry_count. Only the field-offset conventions (menu+44, menu+32) and the general shape carried over from the template.

notes: Read the raw assembly directly: page=state->+8, menu=Data_03001f2c, combined=page*5+state->+16(entry_count), state->+24=combined; Func_08015270(*(menu+44)); WaitFrames(1) [Func_080030f8]; combined=state->+24 (re-read); flag_val=*(u16*)(menu+combined*2+456); if(flag_val!=0) Func_08015080((flag_val&0x1ff)+(s32)&Value_00000075, *(menu+44), 0, 0); then a do-while row=0..4, y=1,3,5,7,9, each iteration calling Func_080a2268(*(menu+32), 1, y, 14, 1, row==entry_count?14:15) -- confirmed the two branches share reg-arg4=14 and stack-arg5=1 and only differ in the final stack argument (14 vs 15).

The Value_00000075 spelling (address-of-symbol rather than a plain +0x75) was inferred from the same evidence pattern as the sibling owners in this batch: 0x75 fits an 8-bit movs immediate yet the reference still spends a pool load on it, which only makes sense if it's really `(s32)&Value_00000075`, matching this project's established Value_XXXXXXXX convention for message-id bases.

Reordering `page = state->8` to be read before `menu = Data_03001f2c` (matching the reference's read-page-before-deref-menu sequence) improved the score marginally (wrong_instructions 52->50); the call sequence, argument counts/values, and branch condition all already match structurally. Remaining differences are concentrated in register-role choices for the two `ldr [pc,#108]`-textual-offset (but distinct real address) pool constants feeding the `(flag_val & 0x1ff) + base` expression, and in the ordering of a few stack stores inside the two Func_080a2268 call sites.

This reads as a scheduling/register-role gap on an already-correct algorithm rather than a missing behavior; worth another pass experimenting with the AND/ADD operand order (e.g. `(s32)&Value_00000075 + (flag_val & 0x1ff)` swapped) and with computing the row==entry_count call's stack args in the reference's exact instruction order before another measurement.
